title: THE NIGHT SCHOOL FOR MONSTERS

rounds.summary: The most human and most urgent of the ten, and the one where force is most tempting and most clearly wrong. Both sides hold a coherent, sympathetic account: Headmaster Vale survived the first uncontrolled surge and believes rehearsal outside the walls gambles with innocent lives; the students want freedom before captivity erases who they might become; the townspeople have real injuries. No one is a straw opponent, and the strongest objection (no simulation has reproduced the eclipse amplification) is a true argument. The decisive idea, making the feared alternative testable under shared control so change comes from evidence and relationship rather than surrender, is surprising beforehand and clear afterwards, and it asks for acts on the page (a student naming fear without punishment, Vale witnessing one student's control) rather than a speech. The positive result is concrete: a controlled drill, a graduated freedom charter Vale signs by choice, students who choose continued training, restitution for the injured without a demand to forgive.

R14 preflight. Aim: prevent an armed eclipse-night confrontation and establish a safe, voluntary path from indefinite confinement to civic life for Northwall's young superhumans. Counterpart goals: Headmaster Vale wants no one else harmed after surviving the first uncontrolled surge and believes an unrepeatable eclipse makes freedom an unacceptable experiment; the students want to become people before captivity decides that danger is their permanent identity; Mara Tern wants the injured town protected and materially repaired, not asked to forgive for the sake of a hopeful ending. Strongest objection appears directly: the school's earlier claim of control failed without eclipse amplification, leaving real bodies and livelihoods damaged, so no survivor owes trust to another rehearsal. Decisive understanding: Northwall's dampening system suppresses visible expression and emotional language while storing the force it claims to remove; each student has specific early signals that create a usable warning window when they are allowed to name them. Love in action: Illuminara listens to the injured without bargaining, protects students' vetoes, stands inside the practice zone and physically holds a failing structure, yet refuses to become the mechanism that makes freedom safe only while she is present. Earned change: the first voluntary practice fails visibly when Vale's suppression order destroys the warning window; students, town and school then build separate vetoes, mechanical spillways and an observable partner protocol. Positive result: the total-eclipse drill succeeds under stronger amplification, Vale freely signs away unilateral confinement, the town accepts a bounded thirty-day trial, the students retain the choice to leave or continue training, and a protected restitution trust begins repairing harms without demanding forgiveness. Remaining cost: the market injuries remain, the observatory and water system need repair, the town's fear persists, and each future restriction must still be argued person by person. Illuminara's power catches structural loads and shields observers; it does not suppress the students, command the town or manufacture consent.

A strong first draft that follows the stated proof and risk of the selection: the eclipse itself supplies the test, the first practice fails with a visible cost (Vale's suppression order turns the warning into the accident), and Vale, the students and the injured town all keep a real veto. The living core is the warning window: 'My hearing is narrowing... my voice has a middle', the red cord that fuses, Mara closing a lever with her damaged hand, and the painted MONSTERS gate that stops forming a wall. Mara's strongest objection is on the page and is not dissolved by the ending, and the restitution trust is hers to direct without any forgiveness entered. Three bounded problems remain. First, Illuminara's own decisive understanding (the dampening field stores force and hides the signal) is delivered by narration in one paragraph and by a single question; the students supply the signals and the design, so the reader cannot yet say why this story needs her mind rather than only her hands. Second, the hardest obstacle, three hundred armed townspeople agreeing to watch a drill, and the students' own consent, are both resolved offstage in a few sentences, and the crowd has only one voice (Mara) plus a rifleman who is dismissed. Third, at 3,797 words the draft is well above the normal 1,500-2,500 range, the signal call-and-response (hearing narrows / fingers cold / quarry floor) recurs five times in nearly the same form, and the design scene is mostly summary.

Bounded S1 revision answering Claude T02 P1–P3. Vale now observes the green monitor and orange seam together and states the stored-force finding himself after Illuminara designs a consent-preserving test. The town and dormitory decisions occur on the page through Tomas Ren and Lio Venn; both retain specific reasons and bounded refusal. Tomas also speaks before and after the suppression shot and remains accountable. The redesign is reduced to three physical beats, the warning voices differ, four additional students become distinguishable, and the closing project report is removed while the gate image remains.

T03 does what T02 asked. Vale now watches the green monitor and the orange seam together and states the stored-force finding himself, so his later concession is earned by something he saw. Tomas Ren and Lio Venn give the town and the dormitory reasons of their own; the signal call-and-response is no longer one formula (Oren's cold fingers, Suri's narrowing hearing, Pellin's moving shadow); the project report is gone and the story ends on the gate and the painted word. At 3,461 words it is still long, but each scene now carries a choice. Power does not decide the conflict: the observatory failure comes from Vale's own suppression order, the totality drill succeeds because Oren chooses release and Suri and Mara hold the shutter, and Illuminara's body only keeps the frame standing while they do it. Two bounded problems remain, and both are cheap to fix. First, Lio Venn's refusal is overwritten: in scene 5 he declines the drill and his name stays on the plan as a refusal, yet in scene 6 he speaks inside the totality drill with no visible reason for the change. A named, reasoned no is the strongest agency the story gives the dormitory, so it should not quietly lapse. Second, Illuminara's own contribution sags in scene 5, where the redesign is built entirely by Oren, Mara, Suri and Vale and she appears only to say where the plan must be taken. Her diagnostic question in scene 2 and her frame-holding in scene 6 are real, but the reader should see her understanding change one design decision, not just open the way for it. A third, minor craft point (length and a few time and band details) is folded into minor_notes. Ready for AUTHOR_FINAL after P1 and P2; no further revision round is needed if they land.

Final S1 text after Claude T04. Lio Venn remains behind the inner wall with his named refusal intact; no student who said no enters without a visible new choice. Illuminara asks who may stop the drill when the person inside cannot speak and whether that hand may restart suppression; Mara and Suri turn the answer into outside stop-only authority plus a preserved right to a corrected test. The redesign and town assent are compressed, while consent, restitution, the thirty-day boundary and the gate ending remain.

T05 answers all three priority points of T04. Lio Venn's named refusal now survives: he stays behind the inner wall through totality with his name still written under refused, and the late drill uses only Edda, Jori and Pellin, each with a distinct physical tell. Illuminara's understanding now shapes one design decision: her question about who may call stop when the person inside cannot speak, and whether that hand may restart suppression, becomes the outside stop-only authority and Suri's preserved right to a corrected test, which the final drill then uses. The redesign scene is shorter and each retained line carries a choice, an objection or a physical test. Vale's copper band is now carried and placed, and the eclipse timing is consistent (totality from 23:56, light back at 00:08). Remaining costs are on the page: Tomas Ren's shot, Mara's refusal to give forgiveness, the four who sign neither and keep the right to decide later.

final_critic_line: On an eclipse night, Illuminara asks the question that lets frightened students and an injured town replace a suppression drill with a test every one of them can stop, and the last gate opens both ways.

evaluation.note: Two genuine isolated, source-bound READER_APPEAL_R1 judgments; exact 50/50 arithmetic mean opened only after the valid metadata-only DAY_FREEZE.
